body.x: AU Inc. (CEO Beak-Hyun Kim) participated in the 'Startup Zone' at the Eureka Park K-STARTUP integrated hall of 'CES 2023' in Las Vegas, USA from January 5 (Thursday) to 8 (Sunday, local time) for a total of 4 days.

Founded in 2019, AU specializes in developing and supplying radars as well as sensors for the interiors and exteriors of automobiles. In particular, the startup owns radar technology that can use millimeter wavelengths to detect vital signs such as passengers’ breathing and heart rates. With its independently obtained sensor technology and its wide application range, AU plans to expand their solutions from RFIC design to signal processing and target detection to provide the so-called “Full Custom” design service.

In this exhibition, AU introduced its In-cabin Passenger Detecting Radar. This solution detects and measures passenger’s vital signs such as breathing and heart rate in real time to check their conditions. It can also collect detailed information such as the number and location of passengers, without missing passengers seated in blind spots, by using a radar sensor that can penetrate obstacles.

The In-cabin Passenger Detection Radar is designed to send a notification to the interlocked smartphone app as soon as an abnormality occurs in the passenger’s vital sign to enable immediate action. This can prevent accidents that might occur to the vulnerable such as infants/children, persons with disability, and the elderly when left in the vehicle. Furthermore, it is a more economic choice than traditional ultrasonic sensors or weight sensing sensors.

According to a representative from AU, “Every year, more than 50 accidents occur in which children are left in vehicles in the summer and end up dying. To prevent such tragic accidents, our radar uses a technology that detects the passenger's vital signs.” “Our intention is to precisely detect the number of passengers and their seating locations to link them with seat belts and advanced airbag systems, creating a safer vehicle environment.”

“We are also working on high-definition imaging radars that use radar sensors in the 77 GHz band to accurately detect driving conditions.” The representative added, “With this proprietary technology, we aims to identify new partners for the domestic market as well as for the North American and European markets.”

‘CES’ is the world’s biggest IT trade show and is a place where one can see the direction and trends of the appliance industry of the entire world. Hosted by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), it is held annually in Las Vegas, USA in January. Having reported on CES for 17 consecutive years, AVING News started reporting news of CES to the entire world since 2006, and conducted ‘BEST OF CES’, which chose the most innovative product and technology, and ‘BEST OF MADE IN KOREA, which chose the best innovative company in Korea. In addition, it vividly relayed on-site issues in CES through ‘AVING LIVE’.

The K-STARTUP Joint Pavilion featured joint participation of institutions like the Korea Institute of Startup & Entrepreneurship Development, Seoul Business Agency, and Seoul Digital Foundation, as well as 51 Korean innovative companies, to enter the US market and discover global partners. In addition, university student supporters of CES 2023 chosen by each university (Kyunghee, Kookmin, Sogang, Chung-Ang) matched to participating companies based on their respective majors and fields of business.
